summary: Agent delivered a partial solution with wrong log base in KLD/scanning and incorrect motif insertion in generate_dna; verifier correctly failed with 1/3 steps passing.

judge_verdict.summary: Agent delivered a partial solution with wrong log base in KLD/scanning and incorrect motif insertion in generate_dna; verifier correctly failed with 1/3 steps passing.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure (TN): the verifier correctly scored binary_reward 0 with only step 76.1 passing and fractional reward 0.333 because compute_kld failed its assertion and scan_sequence returned None where an integer position was expected [1]. The task required KLD and window log-odds against a uniform 0.25 background, PWM motif insertion into a uniformly drawn sequence, and repeated sliding-window scanning against scale·KLD [2][6], but the agent implemented compute_kld and scan_sequence with np.log2 rather than natural logarithms [3], whereas the reference uses np.log throughout [4], yielding a KLD of roughly 14.59 instead of the expected 10.11 on the canonical PWM fixture. The agent's generate_dna kept the background at length N and overwrote a motif window with p drawn from randint(0, N-L) [3], instead of splicing a PWM-sampled motif into a uniform length-N draw at p in [0, N-1] and building the reverse complement from that splice as the reference does [5], so chained step-76.4 tests that call generate_dna then scan_sequence could not recover the HDF5 target binding positions [6][1]. After an initial failed heredoc shell write, the agent saved solution.py via write_file and declared the implementation complete without executing any self-tests [7], even though its own reasoning noted ambiguity about log bases and insertion semantics. The task was not genuinely accomplished and the verifier's FAIL is fair.
